Counts are per-orbit comparisons that clear the summed reference-inclusive envelope; "unres." counts those that do not; ρ is the median of the per-orbit ratios of the comparator's error to the interior member's. The oracle is a post-hoc lower envelope, not a policy

label: tab:oracle-ultra
claim: The oracle panel re-run at the third tolerance level. Errors are the texttt tighter-level errors of Table ref tab:span-oracle and do not move; each envelope is rebuilt from that policy's tighter-to-ultra self-difference plus the reference's. "unres." counts comparisons that do not clear the summed envelope. A flip is a resolved verdict reversing its winner; a comparison passing from undecided to resolved is not a flip

label: tab:bin-control-budget
claim: The bin-resolution control at the budget-calibrated point, on the ten resolved β=1 comparisons of widest degree span. Every parameter of the interior member is held at its archived value; only the quantization is removed. A reversal is a resolved verdict changing its winner; lost resolution is a resolved comparison falling below the summed envelope

label: tab:equal-work

label: tab:bracket-shift

label: tab:equal-work-tighter-ext

label: tab:accounting-ladder

label: tab:apolune-posthoc

label: tab:band-misses

label: tab:designC-ladder

The two rows of each budget are the nominal per-call and the realized total quadratic work accountings. Counts are resolved comparisons under the reference-inclusive resolution rule; ρ is the median per-orbit error ratio

label: tab:three-design

label: tab:strata-panel
claim: The propagated strata at the declared budget, realized total quadratic work and the nominal per-call budget it is matched on. Counts are resolved comparisons under the reference-inclusive resolution rule. The coverage designs are reported in Sections ref sec:span-sweep, ref sec:designC and the main text; a stratum's sub-box lies inside their box, so the two are read side by side and never summed

label: tab:operational-cap-control
claim: The endpoint comparison with the ceiling at the adopted reference degree and with it lifted, decomposed by whether the capped run's schedule reached the ceiling on that orbit. Each pair is the same 64 orbits under the two reference degrees. ρ is the median per-orbit fixed-to-radial error ratio over all orbits of the block; "work" is the median realized total quadratic work of the radial endpoint over that of the constant degree, so a value above one means the radial side spent more. Only the two budgets where the ceiling binds on more than a handful of orbits carry a decomposition

label: tab:endpoint-equal-work
claim: The radial endpoint against a constant degree matched on realized total quadratic work rather than nominal per-call work. ρ is the median per-orbit work-matched-to-radial error ratio, so above one favors the radial endpoint

label: tab:operational-panel
claim: The operational elliptical population at the declared budget, in the columns every other population is reported in. Perilune 80--120 km, apolune 700--2500 km, eccentricity 0.145--0.395: outside the frozen factor box the coverage designs sample, which the asterisked row alone in this paper marks. The coverage designs are repeated below the rule for reference and are not pooled with it

label: tab:ladder-geometry

label: tab:span-ladder-primary
claim: The allocation response along the paired apolune ladder. (a) Radial endpoint against its equal-budget constant degree, by apolune level and budget; orbit counts are per cell, as a range where the levels in a column differ, and turnover is the level pair the verdict changes between. label: tab:block-replication

label: tab:ladder-interior-rematch

label: tab:ladder-uncapped-rematch
claim: The ceiling-free ladder's interior panel under the scoring-tolerance match, per apolune level and never pooled across levels

label: tab:jgcd-cross-solution
claim: The budget comparison at β = 1 under one set of definitions, on two GRAIL solutions produced independently from shared tracking data. The primary-field rows are the archived populations re-scored with the campaign's statistic, not transcribed from the archived summaries

label: tab:jgcd-cross-solution-medians
claim: Median ratios for the same three populations. ρ _F < 1 means the radial allocation has the smaller force defect; ρ _X > 1 means it has the larger trajectory error

label: tab:jgcd-budget-grid
claim: Force-metric ranking against budget on both gravity solutions. "wins" counts orbits on which the radial rule has the smaller defect. A budget is censored where a policy reaches the adopted reference degree and its defect is identically zero, so the uncensored count falls as the budget rises

label: tab:jgcd-budget-ladder
claim: The two metrics on the same population of the cross-solution field, budget by budget. The force metric reverses across the grid; the trajectory metric does not. Counts are over the resolved comparisons

label: tab:jgcd-budget-ladder-primary
claim: The same ladder on the primary solution, pooled over both confirmatory designs and re-scored from archived trajectories with no new integration. The pooling is one of the two the paper allows: these counts measure what the censor removes rather than rank the policies, whose design-separated verdicts are in Table ref tab:budget-trajectory-pareto. Rows differ from 2× 64 because the censor described above drops a budget wherever the radial schedule reaches the reference degree (JprimCensoredAtCross at β=0.75, JprimCensoredAtUnit at β=1), and design B carries no archived record at β=1.25. Point estimates are at the tighter level where Table ref tab:budget-trajectory-pareto scores at tight

label: tab:jgcd-full-dynamics
claim: The budget comparison under DE440/MOON_PA dynamics with third-body gravity and eclipsed SRP, across budgets, population sizes, designs, and the two calibration arms. "Resolved in both" counts orbits whose comparison resolves under gravity-only and full dynamics; "sign agrees" counts those of them whose trajectory-metric ordering is unchanged. label: tab:jgcd-geometry
claim: The wide-elliptic population under DE440/MOON_PA with third-body gravity and eclipsed SRP. ρ is the median radial-over-constant trajectory-error ratio, so a value below one favors the radial endpoint; it is the reciprocal of the main text's ρ _budget. "Resolved in both" counts orbits resolving under gravity-only and full dynamics alike
